title: The SELECT Squeeze
subtitle: Pizza Palace's billing system is pulling too much data
conceptSummary: You can rename columns in results using AS: SELECT total_price AS amount gives the column a friendly name.

dialogue.text: Welcome to SQL Streets! Here, every query is an investigation. The Pizza Palace billing system needs a clean receipt — just order ID and amount, with a friendly column name.
Use AS to rename columns. 'total_price AS Amount'. It's called an alias. Very detective-y.

teachMoment.title: Column Aliases with AS
teachMoment.body:
Rename columns in your output using AS:

SELECT order_id, total_price AS amount FROM orders

The column in the result shows as 'amount' instead of 'total_price'. Great for clean reports!

task.instruction: Select order_id (as 'Order Number') and total_price (as 'Amount Paid') from the orders table.
task.startingQuery:
SELECT order_id AS 'Order Number',
       total_price AS 'Amount Paid'
FROM orders
task.solution: SELECT order_id AS 'Order Number', total_price AS 'Amount Paid' FROM orders

hints.text: After each column name, add AS then the alias in quotes.
Pattern: SELECT col AS 'Alias' FROM table
SELECT order_id AS 'Order Number', total_price AS 'Amount Paid' FROM orders

winDialogue.text: Perfect billing report! And look — order 1001 paid with SHADOW42 discount. The discount saves exactly 15%.
15% is the employee discount rate. Someone is using a staff discount code illegally. Investigate.

storyBeat: SHADOW42 is an employee discount code. Someone either stole it or IS an employee. The pizza shop owner confirms only 3 employees have access. The net is tightening.
